output.summary: KEP-995 proposes adding kubeadm support for joining Windows worker nodes to a cluster, via a PowerShell script that installs kubelet, kubeadm and wins, plus DaemonSets for kube-proxy and Flannel. Its status is implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: Joining a Windows node to a cluster currently requires hand-written scripts to download binaries and write config files, which the KEP calls a major pain point for Windows adoption. The KEP aims to give Windows the same single-command join and reset that kubeadm provides on Linux. Scope is limited to Windows worker nodes; container runtime installation, kubeadm init, and control-plane join are excluded.

alternatives.option: Continue using a set of scripts to download Kubernetes binaries and write config files
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this approach 'has proven to be cumbersome and is a huge pain point for Windows adoption.'

alternatives.option: Install the container runtime (Docker or containerd) as part of this work
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal: 'Installing the Container Runtime (e.g. Docker or containerd)'.

alternatives.option: Implement kubeadm init or kubeadm join --control-plane for Windows
alternatives.why_not: Both are explicit non-goals of this KEP.

evidence.quote: The current solution is to create a set of scripts to download Kubernetes binaries and write their config files, but this has proven to be cumbersome
The motivation for this KEP is to provide a tool to allow users to take a Windows machine and join it to an existing Kubernetes cluster with a single command.
It should be noted that at this time, this document only proposes enablement of support for Windows worker nodes using kubeadm.
Create and maintain a Powershell script to install kubelet, kubeadm and [wins](https://github.com/rancher/wins/)
